title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.2): for a modular-dimension-0 'MD graph' G, the groupoid S_0T_G reduces, via the product formula (2) and the change of structure group (1), to the one-vertex case S_0T_{0,I} with |I| = 3. Take the I-marked projective line P^1_I over C. For each i in I, T_i is the U-torsor of unit tangent rays at i, where U = {|z| = 1}. Their product PU_{0,I} = prod_i T_i is a U^I-torsor. Each orientation alpha of the 3-element set I gives a canonical trivialisation, hence a point alpha-bar in PU_{0,I}. This yields an embedding (3) omega(I) -> PU_{0,I}, where omega(I) is the 2-element set of orientations. It is equivariant for the diagonal map (4) {±1} -> {±1}^I ⊂ U^I.

This page:
(i) (3) and (4) are compatible with the action of the symmetric group S_I. S_I acts on omega(I) through the signature, and on PU_{0,I} and U^I by transport of structure.
(ii) Definition: S_0T_{0,I} is the full subgroupoid of the fundamental groupoid Pi_1(PU_{0,I}) on the object set omega(I). It is a connected groupoid with two objects. Its vertex groups are Z^I = pi_1(U^I), so it is a Z^I-groupoid in the sense of p.2.
(iii) Grothendieck wants a purely algebraic description. He takes the standard universal covering group R -> U, t -> exp(2 i pi t), with exact sequence 0 -> Z -> R -> U -> 0, and its I-th power (S_I): 0 -> Z^I -> R^I -> U^I -> 0. He observes that the torsor structure of PU_{0,I} under the topological group U^I determines its topology. So the fundamental groupoid should be expressible using only (S_I) and the torsor structure.
(iv) He begins the general setting: an extension of topological groups (6) 0 -> pi -> T~ -> T -> 0, with pi discrete, pi ⊂ T~°, and T~° simply connected. Typically T is a compact torus and pi is free of finite type.

The next page completes this. For a T-torsor P, Pi(x,y) = T~_{y-x}, the fibre of T~ over y - x, with composition given by addition in T~. Abstractly, an abelian extension E of Gamma by pi together with a Gamma-torsor gives a connected pi-groupoid.

Applied here: the difference between the two objects alpha-bar and (-alpha)-bar is (-1,...,-1) in U^I. Its lifts form (1/2 + Z)^I. So S_0T_{0,I} is the connected 2-object groupoid with automorphism groups Z^I and Hom(alpha, -alpha) = (1/2 + Z)^I. Equivalently, its 'total arrow group' is the index-2 overgroup Z^I + Z(1/2,...,1/2) of Z^I. Geometrically, Z^I is generated by Dehn twists around the three punctures, and the half-integral arrows are the 'half-twist' moves exchanging the two orientations, i.e. the two hemispheres of the real structure. This is the elementary genus-0, 3-point brick of Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower with tangential (unit-tangent-ray) base points.
errors: No mathematical errors. The conditions in (6) are slightly redundant: once T~° is simply connected and pi is discrete, T~° -> T° is the universal cover. The condition pi ⊂ T~° is what makes T~ the 'fundamental group extension'. The page stops before the general formula, which comes on p.4.

ideas.what: Teichmüller-groupoid building block S_0T_{0,I}: full subgroupoid of the fundamental groupoid of the torus of unit tangent rays at the 3 marked points, on the two orientation base points
ideas.modern_name: Genus-0 three-holed-sphere piece of the Teichmüller (Lego) groupoid with framed/tangential base points; framed (decorated) moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) for the Teichmüller tower; tangential base points Deligne 1989; framed versions e.g. Bakalov–Kirillov 2000, Moore–Seiberg
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §§2-3 describes the Teichmüller tower and Dehn-twist generators qualitatively; this explicit unit-tangent-ray torsor construction does not appear there as far as I know

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a torsor under a topological abelian group, computed algebraically from the universal covering extension: Pi(x,y) = T~_{y-x}
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of a torsor / groupoid associated to a group extension and a torsor (action/quotient groupoid)
ideas.where_published: Similar ideas on torsors and groupoids appear in SGA1/SGA4 and Pursuing Stacks in general form

ideas.what: S_I-equivariance via the signature on orientations, compatible with diagonal {±1} -> U^I
ideas.modern_name: Equivariance of tangential base points under symmetric-group action

missed.claim: The discrete genus-0 Teichmüller brick is described as a Z^I-groupoid built from unit tangent rays at the marked points, with the two orientations of P^1 as base points. Its arrows between them form (1/2+Z)^I, a 'half-twist' structure. This anticipates the framed/extended-surface Teichmüller groupoids (Bakalov–Kirillov) and tangential base points (Deligne), but in a purely algebraic torsor language. A specialist may find the clean formulation with two orientation objects and an index-2 extension of the twist group nice, but it is essentially known.
missed.quote: définis S_0T_{0,I} comme le sousgroupoïde du groupoïde fondamental de PU_{0,I} induit sur ω(I) comme ens. d'objets
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck was already working with framed / tangential base points and twist torsors in his Teichmüller-tower program. This is of historical interest for crediting the 'Lego' formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: A definitional, largely routine page: torsor fundamental groupoids via universal covering extensions. Its only interest is historical, showing how Grothendieck set up the genus-0 building block with tangent-ray torsors and orientation base points, which is close to later framed Teichmüller groupoids.
transcription_corrections: 'opère sur u(I)' and 'induit sur u(I)': read ω(I), the set of orientations of I.
'(qui opère sur ω(I) par la [?])': the illegible word is 'signature'.
'le {+groupe+} [-revêtement-] universel standard': the insertion above the line reads 'groupe' (or 'revêtement' kept); the sense is the universal covering group R of U.
The label of the first exact sequence may be (S_1) or (S_0); it is the I = singleton case.

Lines around 'détermine sa topologie' read roughly: 'Notons que PU_{0,I} est un torseur sous le groupe topologique U^I, [structure algébrique] qui détermine sa topologie. Je vois qu'une construction purement algébrique donne le groupoïde fondamental de cet espace (et sa structure), en utilisant seulement (S_I) et la structure de torseur.'
'considérons une structure d'extension de groupes topologiques' is likely 'considérons une extension de groupes topologiques'.
